units: pixels (original 2560x1440 resolution) and seconds; no metric scale estimated

camera.motion: static (mean abs diff of 4 background corner patches vs frame 0 <= 0.51 gray levels in every frame; see camera_check.csv)
camera.view: oblique, looking down onto an infinite light-grey floor (studio cyclorama); no horizon visible - the floor darkens toward the top of the image (far floor), light vignette
camera.perspective_cues: ground plane only (no lines, markings or vanishing points). The whale casts a soft shadow onto the floor below/right of it; the whale floats above the floor (it does not touch it). Moving up in the image = moving away from the camera on/over the floor.
camera.focal_length: unknown - estimate from the question's depth_info + a known size

objects.name: whale
objects.description: humpback whale (dark blue-grey back, lighter grey/white belly and fluke underside, long pectoral flippers). The only animal / moving object.
objects.visible_frames: 0-71 (all). Fluke partly cut off by the bottom image border in frames 8-39 (flag tail_cut/occluded in whale.csv). Head region looks faded/semi-transparent (render artefact) but is included in the mask.
objects.motion: swims steadily toward the upper-left of the image (away from the camera, roughly parallel to the floor - its shadow moves by about the same pixel vector) while doing one fluke stroke: tail sweeps DOWN (toward bottom of image) frames 1-~29, then UP frames ~29-71, ending with the body nearly straight/horizontal and the fluke at upper right.
objects.reference_point_note: the rig origin is not visible. Best proxies: whale_head.csv (template-tracked head patch, rigid-body translation, smooth) and the mask centroid cx,cy in whale.csv (biased by the tail flap). Root translation ~= head-track translation.

head_track_summary_px.per_frame_step: about 2.2-2.9 px/frame toward upper-left, frames 2-71; zero between frames 0 and 1

objects.apparent_size_change: head/front-body SIFT similarity scale vs frame 0: 0.994 (f5), 0.989 (f10), 0.976 (f15), 0.967 (f20), 0.955 (f25), 0.943 (f30), 0.932 (f35), 0.914 (f40), 0.886 (f45), ~0.86 (f50-55), ~0.84-0.85 (f65-71; noisy, body bending/pitch also contributes). The whale gets smaller as it swims away; see head_scale.csv
objects.pectoral_flipper_left_frame0_px: hanging flipper at image left of the body, from ~(1070,635) to ~(1025,1110): ~475 px long (rough, by eye)

objects.name: whale_shadow
objects.description: soft dark-grey shadow of the whale on the floor, below / lower-left to lower-right of the whale
objects.visible_frames: 0-71; its lower part is cut by the bottom border in all frames (cut_by_bottom_border flag)
objects.note: centroid of gray<150 pixels outside the whale mask below y=500; displacement f0->f71 (-168,-129) px, similar to the head displacement (-163,-116)

objects.name: floor
objects.description: infinite light-grey ground plane / cyclorama, no texture or markings
objects.extent: fills the frame; no measurable features

events.event: video start, frames 0 and 1 identical (no motion between them)
fluke tip reaches bottom border (fluke partially out of frame)
tail downstroke ends / reverses to upstroke (minimum of whole-image frame difference at frames 27-28; fluke hidden below border so exact reversal estimated 27-30)
fastest tail upstroke (tail-tip y steps ~33-35 px/frame, frame difference peak)
end of clip, tail still rising slowly, body nearly straight

files.tracks/whale.csv: per-frame whale mask: centroid, bbox, area, PCA axis length/width/angle, max tip-to-tip span and its endpoints, topmost point, head point, tail tip, head-to-tail distance, occluded/tail_cut flags
files.tracks/whale_head.csv: per-frame head-patch template track (head_x, head_y, match_score)
files.tracks/whale_shadow.csv: per-frame shadow blob centroid / bbox / area
files.head_scale.csv: apparent scale of head region vs frame 0
